title: The text discusses the challenges faced by African countries in achieving food security and the impact of foreign aid on agricultural policies. It highlights the dependency on imported grains, which exacerbates hunger and economic issues. The author argues that modernization of agriculture is not the only solution, citing successful examples from Tanzania and Ghana that relied on peasant-based agriculture. Additionally, it addresses the severe drought crisis in the Sahel region, where farmers struggle with low liquidity and lack of resources, leading to malnutrition and health issues among vulnerable populations. The text emphasizes the need for sustainable agricultural practices and improved access to health care in these regions.
